newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen stabilising next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen stabilising next week.

text.p: Polish shares are expected to stay flat next week as the bourse hits a consolidation phase after having risen for most of the month.
Analysts said the main WIG index, which rose one percent this week to 14,735.5 points, could ease slightly but would likely find support between 14,000 and 14,500 points.
"Until companies' September earnings results are released in mid-October I don't think we have any reason to expect a significant move," said Wojciech Kossuth, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
Analysts said if September's numbers matched those of the previous two months in proving better than the first half's disappointing figures, the overall market mood could stay good.
They said investors would also be waiting to see if year-on-year inflation after September fell below 20 percent and gave reason for an interest-rate cut.

Analysts said this was still possible after food prices rose 1.4 and 1.3 percent in September's first two thirds respectively, but that higher food and fuel prices during the fourth quarter still threatened.
Analysts said another threat was the political situation both domestically and in nearby Russia.

They said investors might be holding back as the parties in Poland's governing coalition, the Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and Polish Peasant Party (PSL), clash over who gets which ministries upon the forthcoming cabinet reorganisation.
But they said a good sign was the PSL's acceptance on Thursday of a gradual replacement of individual ministers rather than the dismissal of the whole cabinet and a prompt formation of a new one.
Some analysts also said Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery due in six weeks was creating uncertainty and thereby dampening buying on the Polish bourse.
"The uncertainty has been extended for about two months, which can hinder growth," said Adam Drozdowski, an analyst at Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) brokerage.
Bank Komunalny, the main market's top gainer this week, surged 27.1 percent after having started trade last week 59 percent above issue, but analysts said profit-taking loomed.
